matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After you have a candidate transformed equation, compute the integer values of both sides using standard Roman‑numeral conversion and verify that they are equal. Skipping this step can let an equation that looks syntactically correct but is arithmetically false pass.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Right after you generate a possible equation, before you output it.
matchstick.example: Accepting a transformation that yields ‘XVI = IX + VII’ without noticing that 16 ≠ 9 + 7.

matchstick.title: Preserve valid numeral shapes
matchstick.principle: When a stick is removed from a Roman numeral, the remaining strokes must still form a standard numeral; likewise, adding a stick must produce a standard numeral. This prevents creating symbols such as a lone diagonal or an empty character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During each stick relocation, check the source and destination characters after the move.
matchstick.example: Removing the only vertical stick from an isolated ‘I’, leaving an empty glyph.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you may only place it in a location that respects that orientation. Ignoring orientation creates impossible glyphs.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When deciding where to attach the moved stick, consider its original orientation and the allowed orientations of the target character.
matchstick.example: Trying to turn a vertical stick into a diagonal line to make a ‘V’ from an ‘I’.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single stick move can affect at most the source character (which loses a stick) and the destination character (which gains a stick). No other characters may be altered in the same move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When planning a stick relocation, ensure only the two involved characters change.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from ‘X’ to ‘V’ and also altering the ‘+’ sign in the same step.

matchstick.title: Maintain a valid equality
matchstick.principle: The equality sign must remain exactly two horizontal sticks; you cannot remove, add, or modify it, nor use it as a source or destination. This guarantees the equation stays an equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider any stick move, never involve the ‘=’ sign.
matchstick.example: Removing one horizontal bar from ‘=’ to turn it into ‘‑’, which violates the rule.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: Use known one‑stick transformations (e.g., I↔II, V↔X) that keep both characters valid after the move. This limits the search space to feasible numeral changes.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change a numeral’s value, consult the list of allowed one‑stick transformations.
matchstick.example: Attempting to turn ‘V’ into ‘L’ by moving a single stick, which is not a valid one‑stick transformation.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final output must be a single line that starts with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the full corrected equation, and it must be the last such line in the response. Any deviation (missing prefix, missing ‘=’, extra text) causes rejection.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a valid transformed equation, before you submit the answer.
matchstick.example: Outputting just ‘XVI - IX = VII’ without the required prefix, or omitting the ‘=’ sign.

matchstick.title: Accurate parsing of the original equation
matchstick.principle: Read the given equation carefully and record each numeral and operator exactly as they appear before planning any stick moves. Misidentifying an operator (e.g., seeing a ‘+’ where there is a ‘‑’) leads to impossible transformations.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the very start of solving the puzzle, before any manipulation.
matchstick.example: Assuming the equation contains a ‘+’ and trying to move its vertical stick, when the original equation actually has a ‘‑’ operator.

matchstick.title: Within‑character diagonal repositioning
matchstick.principle: You may relocate a diagonal stick within the same numeral, effectively turning X into V (or V into X) without affecting other characters. This respects orientation and keeps the character valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a transformation requires changing X to V (or vice versa) while staying within a single character.
matchstick.example: Trying to turn X into V by moving a diagonal to a different character, which violates the within‑character rule.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a ‘‑’ creates a ‘+’, and removing the vertical stick from a ‘+’ yields a ‘‑’. This lets you flip the sign of an operation with a single stick move, provided the resulting operator is valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change a ‘+’ to ‘‑’ or vice versa as part of achieving a correct equality.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from ‘+’ but placing it in a location that does not form a proper ‘‑’, resulting in an invalid operator.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model often focuses on making the symbols look correct and forgets to check whether the resulting numbers actually satisfy the equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the integer values of both sides after a proposed transformation and confirm they are equal before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: When moving a stick, the model may ignore the set of allowed Roman‑numeral glyphs, producing shapes like a lone diagonal or an empty character.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, verify that both the source and destination characters correspond to a standard Roman numeral.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may produce operators that are not among the allowed set (+, -, =), e.g., a single horizontal line where a plus sign is required, or a malformed symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that any operator created by adding or removing sticks is exactly one of '+', '-', or '='.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effective removal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes removes a stick from a character without placing it elsewhere, effectively deleting a stick, which violates the ‘move exactly one stick’ rule.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure that every stick you take from a source character is placed onto a destination character, preserving the total stick count.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may omit the required prefix, forget the equality sign, or place extra text after the answer line, causing the parser to miss the solution.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Output exactly one line that starts with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the full corrected equation, and make it the last such line.
